Well, looks like we've hit a dead end. The portal puzzle was a clever idea for an intelligence test—Blish really knows what he's doing with the portal tech. Unfortunately, it looks like the specimens aren't showing any special intellectual capacity. I wasn't the only one expecting positive results due to the Balthazar energy absorbed by Kralkatorrik.

A note: I'm starting to worry about housing the Branded specimens here. It's not just that they're extremely aggressive. I think there's strategy involved in their behavior. The other day, it really seemed like they were trying to trick me into leaving my notes in their lockup—notes that include the codes to the locks. Am I being paranoid?

A thought: maybe we should be testing their strategic/tactical capacities rather than their intellect?

Dragon Bash? Dragon? Bash? I'm beside myself with confusion and rage. Do those bilge-swilling simpletons in Lion's Arch think any public amusement featuring dragons is a well-thought out idea? I hear they've decorated with a dragon hologram flying above the city. Isn't that just festive of them? I swear, if it looks like Kralktorrik, I'll devote the rest of my life to ruining that sea-soaked burg for trivializing Snaff's death. Good thing I don't have to step foot in there to smash dragon piñatas, burn effigies, and battle dragon holograms. I hear they're scattering piñatas in the cities and the rest around outside. That's acceptable, but only just.

Why don't you head to Lion's Arch and watch this disaster unfold. It's always good to have a laugh at someone else's idiocy.

—Zojja

Of the many weapons within our enemies' arsenal, spectral agony continues to prove itself the most dangerous and terrible of them all.  
  
Not only does it inflict the most excruciating pain imaginable without causing a single wound, but it also saps the victim's will to fight against it, crushing down upon them until they can no longer think of anything but the pain.  
  
That the mursaat would even devise such a spell speaks volumes about their capacity for cruelty and savagery, and it gives our people every reason to oppose them at every turn. There can be no reasoning with such beings, no peace that can be brokered when such methods are employed.  
  
This council would do well to heed my call on this matter, even in my exile, lest we find ourselves groveling before these foul beings and their ultimate weapon of control. We must act, and act now.  
  
There can be no compromise on this.  
  
—Isgarren

strings.en:
After once again ridding my library of the miserable filth placed by the Ministry of Poor Grammar and Unnecessary Conjunctions, I decided to take one of the specimens back to my personal quarters. For research, of course.

"Purity's Embrace" is as appalling as one would think. It is filled to the brim with the worst smut imaginable—even worse than that Tyrian writer, Snargle Goldclaw.

It started with a particularly...grueling encounter between Reiko and her most "trusted servant." I'll omit graphic and unnecessary details, as to not expel my dinner, but it was egregious.

Each chapter, as told through these horrific, erotic encounters with the she-kappa Reiko, all end with some "message" about the Ministry of Purity's greater impact on "national positivity." It's appalling, really, and I fear that such contrived garbage may find its way into the hands of our youth. There's better smut out there, I assure you.

Should this nonsense persist—both the placement of vile literature in my library and its production—I, Minister Preeda, will be forced to act.
